title: Loans & Marketplace
intro: This screen is the lending engine of BANXUM. It is where you set up the companies that borrow money, build the loans they want, and run those loans from the moment they go live until they are fully repaid or written off.

A quick mental model of the product. Individual investors (called lenders) put money into their BANXUM account. The platform then funds loans to vetted business borrowers. Borrowers repay over time with interest. Lenders earn that interest and can later withdraw.
Borrowers are companies, not people with logins. There is no borrower portal. An admin types in every borrower's details by hand. The borrower never sees this screen.

Two jargon terms you will see everywhere. The primary market is where a brand-new loan is first funded by investors. The secondary market is where an investor who already owns a slice of a loan sells that slice to another investor. This screen handles admin tasks for both.

This page is laid out top to bottom as: key metrics, Loan Originators, Borrowers, Loans, Secondary-market approvals, and Servicing operations. Direct-loan actions - publish, deterministic deadline resolution, cancellation, order release, borrower disbursement, repayments and recovery - live in Manage. Originator-claim Manage actions are deliberately different: review/publish the imported claim, place/release a hold, or record a repayment through a replacement CSV revision.
whatYouDoHere: Add and edit borrower companies, and watch their KYB status (the company-level identity and compliance check).
Create direct BANXUM loan drafts and review status, amount, yield, LTV and funding deadline. New refinancing-loan creation is disabled; legacy refinancing records remain serviceable.

Create and maintain Loan Originators after off-platform KYB/AML, then import existing performing claims with anonymized borrower disclosure, coupon, target effective yield, minimum investment and a fully reconciled schedule/payment CSV. Optionally declare the originator's skin in the game: 0 bps disables the rule; a positive value is the minimum share of current outstanding principal the originator must retain, rounded up to a minor currency unit. The retained slice is never sold and caps every quote and purchase.

Set each direct loan's minimum subscription (default 50% of the financeable principal) while it is a draft. Publication discloses and permanently freezes the threshold. When the funding deadline passes with the minimum met, the loan is closed and made at the amount subscribed; below the minimum the campaign is cancelled and every reservation is refunded.

Open Manage on a loan row to publish it to the marketplace, resolve its passed funding deadline from the stored minimum, cancel it when required, release a stuck investor order, disburse a funded loan to the borrower, or record borrower repayments. Published loans cannot be put into effect through a discretionary manual close.
Approve, reject or remove non-standard secondary-market listings (investor-to-investor resales).

Service live direct loans through their normal repayment/recovery actions. For originator claims, upload a replacement immutable import revision that preserves every historical payment and adds exactly the newly reconciled borrower payment.

figures.caption: The four summary tiles across the top of the Loans screen.
figures.summary: A quick at-a-glance count of borrowers, loans, committed money and loans that need attention. These numbers are derived live from the loaded borrower and loan lists.

kpiTiles.label: Borrowers
kpiTiles.text: The total number of borrower companies currently loaded. The small text underneath shows how many of them 'can transact', meaning their KYB is approved and they have no compliance hold. Only those borrowers can have a loan published. Watch this to know how many companies are cleared to lend to versus still pending.

kpiTiles.label: Loans
kpiTiles.text: The total number of loans loaded, with a sub-count of how many are 'published' (live on the marketplace and open for investors to fund). Watch this to see how much is actively raising money right now.

kpiTiles.label: Committed
kpiTiles.text: The sum of money investors have committed across the loaded loans, shown in minor units (the smallest currency unit, e.g. 100 for 1.00 CHF). This is how much investor money is currently pledged into loans. It is a rough total across mixed currencies in preview data, so treat it as an order-of-magnitude figure.

kpiTiles.label: Risk items
kpiTiles.text: The number of loans whose status is 'late' or 'defaulted'. These are loans where the borrower has missed payments. Watch this closely: a non-zero number means servicing or recovery work is needed.

notes: These tiles are calculated from the lists below them, not from a separate report. If you filter or refresh the tables, the counts can change.

figures.caption: Loan Originators: accounting entities that sell existing final-borrower claims through BANXUM.
figures.summary: Create the Loan Originator before importing any of its claim loans. Originators are onboarded and KYB/AML-reviewed off-platform; they do not receive investor-portal login accounts.

annotations.label: Loan Originators
annotations.text: This table is the source of the legal counterparty and settlement configuration used by imported originator-claim loans. Search by public name, legal name or registration number when records exist.

annotations.label: Refresh
annotations.text: Reloads Loan Originators from the backend after a create or update operation.

annotations.label: Create Loan Originator
annotations.text: Opens the originator form. Complete the legal identity, settlement and off-platform KYB/AML evidence before importing a claim loan owned by this originator.

notes: An originator is not a borrower portal user. It owns an existing final-borrower claim and sells eligible portions of that claim through BANXUM.

Skin in the game is configured per imported claim loan, not globally on this card. A positive basis-point value reserves the required proportion of outstanding principal for the originator and prevents it from being sold.

figures.caption: The Borrowers table: every borrower company and its compliance gate.
figures.summary: Borrowers are companies that admins enter by hand. KYB stands for Know Your Business: the company-level identity, ownership and compliance check (the business equivalent of KYC for a person). A loan to a borrower can only go live if that borrower's KYB is Approved and the borrower has no compliance hold.

annotations.label: Entity column
annotations.text: The borrower company's legal name with its unique ID (UUID) underneath. Click anywhere on a row to select that borrower; the selected row is used as the default when you create a new loan.

annotations.label: Classification column
annotations.text: The borrower's business classification (for example 'Residential real-estate development') with a chip showing whether that text is Public or Internal. Public means investors can read it on the loan page; Internal means only admins see it. The choice is made per borrower in the create/edit form.

annotations.label: KYB column
annotations.text: The company's KYB status, shown as a coloured chip. There are seven possible values: Not started, Pending, Approved, Declined, Manual review, Expired, and Re-verification required. Only 'Approved' (combined with no compliance hold) lets a loan for this borrower be published. Any other value blocks publishing.

annotations.label: Country column
annotations.text: The borrower's country, or a dash if not recorded. Useful for spotting non-Swiss borrowers at a glance.

annotations.label: Financials column
annotations.text: A short summary of the company's self-reported finances: total assets and last-year revenue, in the borrower's chosen financials currency. This is context only; it does not gate anything automatically.

annotations.label: Actions column
annotations.text: Holds the per-row Edit button. Note there is no delete: borrowers cannot be removed from this screen.

annotations.label: Filter borrowers by KYB status
annotations.text: A dropdown to show only borrowers in a chosen KYB status (or 'All KYB statuses'). Use it to quickly find, for example, every company stuck in Manual review.

annotations.label: Refresh button
annotations.text: Reloads the borrower list from the backend. Use it after creating or editing a borrower if the table has not updated on its own.

annotations.label: Create borrower button
annotations.text: Opens a form to enter a new borrower company by hand: legal name, year founded, type, business classification, addresses and contact info (each with a 'public' checkbox that controls whether investors may see it), plus internal-only ownership, bank-account, KYB/AML-observation and financial-risk notes. New borrowers usually start with a Pending KYB status, so you cannot publish a loan for them until KYB is later moved to Approved.

annotations.label: Edit button (row action)
annotations.text: Opens the borrower edit form for that company. This is where KYB status and the compliance hold flag are changed. Moving KYB to Approved and clearing any compliance hold is what unlocks loan publishing for that borrower.

annotations.label: Approved chip
annotations.text: Example of an 'Approved' KYB chip. A borrower in this state, with no compliance hold, is cleared to have its loans published and to receive borrower repayments.

annotations.label: Manual Review chip
annotations.text: Example of a 'Manual review' KYB chip. The company is parked for a human compliance decision. Loans for this borrower cannot be published until KYB reaches Approved.

annotations.label: Public chip
annotations.text: This borrower's classification is marked public, so lenders see the same text on the loan's detail page. Only fields explicitly marked public are ever shown to investors; everything else stays internal.

annotations.label: Internal chip
annotations.text: This borrower's classification is internal-only. Investors see nothing for this field. Internal-only borrower data also includes ownership notes, bank-account details, KYB/AML observations and financial-risk notes - none of these ever reach the investor app.

notes: A borrower is allowed to transact only when KYB equals Approved AND the compliance-hold flag is off. A compliance hold can block an otherwise-approved company.
There is no borrower login anywhere in BANXUM. Every field you see here was typed in by an admin.
The search box (top of the card) lets you find a borrower by legal name, registration number, country or UUID.

figures.caption: The unified Loans table: direct loans and Loan Originator claim loans in one operational view.
figures.summary: Each row is one investor opportunity. Direct loans use a borrower KYB gate and a funding round. Originator claims use an immutable imported schedule, anonymized borrower disclosure, target-yield pricing, immediate claim assignment and an optional originator-retention floor.

annotations.label: Loan / counterparty column
annotations.text: Shows the opportunity title, its borrower or Loan Originator counterparty, and its unique reference. Click a row to select it; Manage always stays pinned to that exact opportunity.

annotations.label: Product column
annotations.text: Distinguishes Direct loans from Originator claims. The two products share an investor-opportunity table but have different creation, publication, settlement and servicing actions.

annotations.label: Status column
annotations.text: The current lifecycle or opportunity status. The server uses this status to decide which Manage actions are available; it is not merely a display label.

annotations.label: Progress column
annotations.text: For a direct loan, shows committed versus financeable principal and the funding percentage. For an originator claim, it shows how much of the eligible claim has been sold while respecting the originator-retention floor.

annotations.label: Yield column
annotations.text: The target annual yield presented to investors. For direct loans this is the contractual investor rate. For originator claims the executable purchase price changes over time so the investor's target yield remains the configured value. Internally percentages use basis points (100 bps = 1%).

annotations.label: LTV column
annotations.text: Loan-to-Value: current loan principal divided by eligible collateral value. A lower LTV means more collateral margin. A dash means the product has no disclosed LTV.

annotations.label: Availability date column
annotations.text: For direct loans this is the funding deadline. For originator claims it is the contractual maturity date; the claim stops being available once it reaches its configured maturity-window cutoff or another terminal condition.

annotations.label: Actions column
annotations.text: Direct loans offer Edit and status-aware Manage actions. Originator claims use their own Manage workflow for imported evidence, publication, holds and replacement repayment revisions. Delete is intentionally unavailable for financial evidence.

annotations.label: Filter loans by status
annotations.text: Narrows the unified table by lifecycle status. Use the search field above it to find a title, borrower, originator, product, status or UUID.

annotations.label: Refresh button
annotations.text: Reloads both product types from the backend after a mutation.

annotations.label: Create direct loan
annotations.text: Creates a draft for a BANXUM-originated direct borrower loan. Select the borrower, principal, yield, term, repayment type, collateral, start date and funding deadline; the server generates and validates the schedule.

annotations.label: Import originator claim loan
annotations.text: Imports a Loan Originator-owned claim from a fully reconciled schedule/payment CSV. The form also captures target investor yield, minimum investment and optional skin-in-the-game basis points. A positive retention value is rounded up to a minor unit and remains unsellable.

annotations.label: Manage button (row action)
annotations.text: Opens the product-specific workflow for the selected row. Direct and originator-claim actions are deliberately separated so imported claim evidence cannot be edited through the direct-loan lifecycle.

annotations.label: Published status chip
annotations.text: Example of a direct loan live in the primary marketplace and accepting investor orders.

annotations.label: Late status chip
annotations.text: Example of a 'Late' chip: at least one installment is 5 or more days past due. If it reaches 16 or more days past due, the status scan moves it to Defaulted. Late loans still accept repayments.

annotations.label: Defaulted status chip
annotations.text: A defaulted direct loan is handled through recovery. Every payment still follows the same server-owned order: Garanta legal costs and recovery fee, penalty, interest, then principal.

notes: Publishing a direct loan checks required fields, schedule conservation, funding deadline and borrower KYB/no-hold status. Publishing an originator claim checks the immutable import, originator status, sellable principal and maturity window.
The universal payment waterfall applies to every product and status: Garanta legal costs and recovery fee, penalty, interest, then principal. Principal is never paid ahead of a due earlier tier.
For an originator claim, imported payment-category columns are reconciliation evidence only. The server recomputes the applied split and rejects a CSV that relabels interest or penalty as principal.
Status is enforced. Invalid product/status operations are rejected even if a client tries to call the endpoint directly.

figures.caption: The Manage dialog: pick the action to apply to this loan.
figures.summary: Clicking Manage on a loan row opens this dialog. The bar at the top restates the loan you are acting on: its status chip, funding deadline, committed versus total amount, and ID. Below it is the action menu - only actions valid for the current status are listed. Draft loans offer Publish; published loans offer Cancel funding, Resolve funding deadline, and Release an order's balance; a funding-close failure offers the same actions so operations can retry or refund; funded loans offer Borrower disbursement; active/late loans offer Record borrower repayment; defaulted loans offer Record a recovery payment.

annotations.label: Dialog title
annotations.text: Names the loan you are managing, so you cannot mix up rows. Everything you do in this dialog applies to this loan only.

annotations.label: Loan context bar
annotations.text: The highlighted status sits inside the loan context bar, alongside the funding deadline and committed/total amounts. Check the whole bar before acting - the menu is built from this status.

annotations.label: Cancel funding
annotations.text: Stops the campaign before close. Reserved balances are released back to investors, pending orders close as not invested, and the loan moves to cancelled. Only valid before funding close. The 'Confirmation required' tag means a summary dialog asks you to confirm before anything runs.

annotations.label: Resolve funding deadline
annotations.text: After the deadline, compares committed principal with the stored minimum subscription under the same loan lock. At or above the minimum it closes at the subscribed amount; below it, it cancels and refunds. There is no discretionary admin partial-close choice. A processing failure removes the loan from public view, preserves reservations and opens an urgent task.

annotations.label: Release an order's balance
annotations.text: Returns one allocated order's reserved balance to its investor without touching the rest of the campaign - used when a single order must be unwound, for example after a validation problem.

annotations.label: Close (X)
annotations.text: Closes the dialog without doing anything. Nothing runs until you pick an action and confirm it inside the form.

notes: The menu is status-aware: a draft loan offers Publish; a published or funding-close-failed loan offers Cancel/Resolve deadline/Release; a funded loan offers Borrower disbursement; an active or late loan offers Record borrower repayment; a Defaulted loan offers Record a recovery payment. The Servicing operations panel below keeps only the status scan and public risk notes.

Dangerous actions carry a 'Confirmation required' tag: after filling the form you still get a summary dialog restating loan, reason and message before the backend is called. Repayments in advance additionally show a preview of the allocation and the old and new schedules.

Publishing is subject to backend gates: borrower KYB approved, no compliance hold, complete loan data, a valid funding deadline, schedule principal equal to the financeable principal, and for refinancing loans a financeable principal not above the remaining outstanding of the original schedule.

figures.caption: Resolve a passed funding deadline from the stored minimum subscription.
figures.summary: The context bar stays visible while the deterministic resolver asks only for an as-of date and scope. The server decides close versus cancellation from the stored minimum under a loan lock. Optional reason/message overrides apply to the below-minimum cancellation path; they cannot change the threshold result.

annotations.label: All actions (back)
annotations.text: Returns to the action menu without running anything. Use it if you picked the wrong action.

annotations.label: Funding resolution as-of date
annotations.text: The Europe/Zurich business date used to decide whether the deadline has passed. Do not future-date it in normal operations.

annotations.label: Scan this loan only
annotations.text: Leave enabled for a targeted retry. Disable only when intentionally resolving every expired published campaign. Failed campaigns are never swept into a broad scan; select them explicitly after fixing the cause.

annotations.label: Resolve funding deadline button
annotations.text: Opens a confirmation summary, then closes at the subscribed amount when the threshold is met or cancels/refunds below it. If processing fails, investor reservations remain unchanged and an urgent operations case is opened.

notes: The exact minimum is rounded up to a whole minor unit. The decision and close/cancellation run under the same loan lock, preventing an allocation from racing the threshold check.
Success, preview-mode and error messages appear at the bottom of the dialog, and the loan table refreshes automatically after a successful action.
In preview/demo mode the buttons record a 'Preview action' note instead of calling the backend.

figures.caption: Secondary-market approvals: the table of investor-to-investor resale listings.
figures.summary: Every secondary-market listing, newest first. The secondary market is where an investor who already owns a slice of a loan sells it to another investor. Standard (performing-loan) listings publish automatically and appear here as 'Active'; non-standard listings (late, defaulted, or otherwise flagged) wait as 'Approval requested' until an admin approves them with a buyer disclosure note. The status filter narrows the table, and the action buttons on each row open a confirmation dialog.

annotations.label: Loan / listing column
annotations.text: The loan the listed slice belongs to, with the listing's own ID underneath.

annotations.label: Seller column
annotations.text: The investor selling the slice (name and email). Buyers never see this - seller identity is redacted on the buyer-facing side - but admins need it here to review the listing.

annotations.label: Price column
annotations.text: The transfer price and whether it is a discount or premium to the current principal. Accrued interest and fees are added at settlement.

annotations.label: Loan status column
annotations.text: The underlying loan's status (Published, Late, Defaulted...). This is what makes a listing 'standard' or 'non-standard': a late or defaulted loan needs your approval and a disclosure note before buyers can see it.

annotations.label: DPD column
annotations.text: Days past due on the underlying loan. A non-zero value is a signal to review carefully and disclose the risk to buyers.

annotations.label: Status column
annotations.text: The listing's own status: Approval requested (waiting for you), Active (visible to buyers), Sold, Rejected, Removed, or Cancelled.

annotations.label: Status filter
annotations.text: Narrows the table to one listing status - for example show only 'Approval requested' to work through the queue of listings needing a decision.

annotations.label: Approve (row action)
annotations.text: On an 'Approval requested' row, opens a dialog to approve the listing. You provide a reason and a buyer disclosure note (shown to buyers as the public disclosure), then confirm. The listing becomes Active and visible to eligible buyers with an extra risk acknowledgement.

annotations.label: Reject (row action)
annotations.text: On an 'Approval requested' row, opens a dialog to reject the listing with a reason. It stays hidden from buyers and the decision is audit-logged.

annotations.label: Remove (row action)
annotations.text: On an 'Active' row, opens a dialog to take a live listing out of buyer visibility with an operational reason - used when a listing must be pulled after it went live.

annotations.label: Approval requested chip
annotations.text: This listing is non-standard and waiting for your decision. Only rows in this state show Approve/Reject.

annotations.label: Active chip
annotations.text: This listing is live and visible to buyers. Active rows show a Remove action; sold, rejected and removed rows show no actions.

notes: Standard (performing-loan) listings publish automatically and never need approval; they appear here as Active so you can still Remove one if needed.
Approving a non-standard listing requires a buyer disclosure note - the public text buyers must read and additionally acknowledge before purchase.
Approve, reject and remove are all confirmed in a dialog and recorded in the audit trail with your reason.
Rejected, removed, sold and cancelled listings stay in the table for evidence but offer no further actions.

figures.caption: Servicing operations: scan loan health and post public notes.
figures.summary: Servicing means running a loan after it is funded. This panel now holds only the status scan and public investor notes for the loan selected in the table above. Borrower repayments (a fixed regular installment amount, or 'Repayment in advance' with a bank date and a preview dialog) and recovery payments on defaulted loans are recorded from the loan row's Manage dialog.

annotations.label: Loan field
annotations.text: The loan being scanned or noted. It defaults to the selected loan but can be changed by search.

annotations.label: Run status scan button
annotations.text: Re-checks the loan's health and updates its status. A loan with an installment 5+ days past due becomes Late; 16+ days past due becomes Defaulted; fully paid becomes Repaid. The scan is the only thing that escalates a loan into Defaulted; recording a repayment never does.

annotations.label: Risk note body field
annotations.text: The text of a public update to investors about this loan (for example explaining a delay). This is the message that gets published when you press Publish public note.

annotations.label: Publish public note button
annotations.text: Posts a public risk note that investors holding this loan can read. Public notes are only allowed on loans that are in an active portfolio status (Funded, Late, Defaulted, Repaid or Written off), not on drafts or unfunded loans.

notes: Borrower repayments are recorded from Manage > 'Record borrower repayment': a regular installment uses the fixed outstanding amount of the next due installment (not editable), and any other amount uses 'Repayment in advance' with a 'Borrower repayment bank date' plus a mandatory preview of the allocation and the old and new schedules. The old warning-acknowledged checkbox for partial/irregular amounts was removed.
Each action uses an idempotency key, so an accidental double-submit is safely ignored rather than processed twice.
Recovery payments on a defaulted loan are recorded from the loan row's Manage dialog (Record a recovery payment), not here.

figures.caption: Manage > Record a recovery payment (defaulted loans only).
figures.summary: The recovery action appears in the Manage dialog only when the loan is Defaulted. Record the gross cash, evidenced costs, optional Garanta recovery fee, and amounts currently due for penalties/default interest and contractual interest. The server derives current principal and applies one fixed order: costs/recovery fee, penalty, interest, then principal. The operator cannot choose or reorder the applied split.

annotations.label: Defaulted status
annotations.text: The recovery action only exists for a Defaulted loan. On any other status the Manage menu does not offer it (repayments on funded or late loans are recorded through Manage > 'Record borrower repayment' instead).

annotations.label: Gross recovered
annotations.text: The total amount recovered on the loan before any deductions - for example proceeds from enforcing collateral.

annotations.label: Externally deducted costs
annotations.text: Costs already taken out before the money reached Garanta (deducted from the gross). Net received = gross minus these.

annotations.label: Third-party costs (from received)
annotations.text: External legal or recovery costs paid out of the received funds. These come off before the Garanta fee and the lender distribution.

annotations.label: Apply Garanta recovery fee
annotations.text: Tick to apply Garanta's recovery fee. A basis-points field appears; the fee is charged on the net-of-third-party base and becomes Garanta revenue.

annotations.label: Outstanding default/penalty interest
annotations.text: Enter the evidence-backed default or penalty interest currently due. It belongs to the Penalty tier and is paid before contractual interest or principal.

annotations.label: Outstanding other penalties
annotations.text: Enter any other evidenced penalties currently due. Together with default/penalty interest, this is the second waterfall tier.

annotations.label: Outstanding contractual interest
annotations.text: Enter contractual interest accrued and still due. The server pays it only after costs/recovery fee and the complete penalty tier.

annotations.label: Record recovery
annotations.text: Opens the confirmation summary, then records the recovery. Affected investor balance lots are credited, holding principal is reduced only by the amount that reaches the final tier, and Garanta recovery fee is posted as revenue.

notes: Recovery is only valid on a Defaulted loan; repayments on funded/late loans go through Manage > 'Record borrower repayment' (fixed installment amount, or 'Repayment in advance' with a bank date for any other amount).
The Net received / Fee / Net to distribute summary mirrors the gross-to-net calculation. A second summary previews the fixed four-tier allocation; there is no editable principal-first split.
Principal is never paid while evidenced costs/recovery fee, penalties/default interest, or contractual interest remain due.
In preview/demo mode the button records a 'Preview action' note instead of calling the backend.
